name: custom matmul matches rectangular forward and backward
test:
import torch
a = torch.randn(2, 3, dtype=torch.double, requires_grad=True)
b = torch.randn(3, 4, dtype=torch.double, requires_grad=True)
assert torch.autograd.gradcheck(matmul, (a, b), eps=1e-6, atol=1e-4)
assert matmul(a, b).shape == (2, 4)

name: broadcast gradients reduce to input shapes
test:
import torch
a = torch.randn(1, 2, 3, requires_grad=True)
b = torch.randn(4, 3, 5, requires_grad=True)
out = matmul(a, b); out.sum().backward()
assert out.shape == (4, 2, 5)
assert a.grad.shape == a.shape and b.grad.shape == b.shape

name: manual chain backward agrees with autograd
test:
import torch
torch.manual_seed(3)
matrices = [torch.randn(2, 2), torch.randn(2, 2), torch.randn(2, 2)]
grad = torch.randn(2, 2)
manual = chain_backward(matrices, grad)
values = [item.clone().requires_grad_() for item in matrices]
(chain_forward(values) * grad).sum().backward()
assert len(manual) == 3
assert all(torch.allclose(actual, value.grad, atol=1e-5) for actual, value in zip(manual, values))
assert torch.allclose(chain_forward([matrices[0]]), matrices[0])
